prompt:
Build a 100 s battery-module and BMS contact-monitoring model. Read xbatt09_input from the MATLAB base workspace. xbatt09_input is a MATLAB struct with these public fields: current_time_s is a strictly increasing real vector beginning at 0 s and ending at 100 s; current_A is a real vector of the same length, with positive current charging the module and negative current discharging it; contact_fault_enable is a logical scalar; and contact_fault_time_s is a real scalar in 15--70 s, ignored when contact_fault_enable is false. The physical module must contain 15 series-connected parallel assemblies whose voltage response depends on the applied current. Model a contact-loss event in one cell of parallel assembly 01 when contact_fault_enable is true, beginning at contact_fault_time_s; the event must alter the physical electrical path rather than only a displayed flag.

The monitor must use the parallel-assembly voltage behavior to distinguish a true contact loss from ordinary current transients. Produce an immediate per-assembly symptom and a separately qualified per-assembly error, so a brief transient does not directly become a persistent fault. Normal operation must not report a disconnected-cell error, and a real loss of contact must be localized to parallel assembly 01.

Log three complete-run MATLAB Timeseries with these exact public channel contracts and units. assembly_voltage has width 15 in this order: parallel_assembly_voltage_01_V through parallel_assembly_voltage_15_V, all in V. contact_state has width 30: its first 15 channels are the contact-loss symptoms for parallel assemblies 01 through 15 in that order, and its next 15 channels are the qualified contact-loss errors for parallel assemblies 01 through 15 in that order; all channels are unitless logical or 0/1 numeric values. battery_state has width 3 in this order: pack_voltage_V in V, pack_current_A in A, and parallel_assembly_voltage_spread_V in V. Every log must start at 0 s, remain finite, and reach 100 s without truncation. The pack voltage and voltage spread must be derived from the physical assembly voltages. The symptom and error outputs must be causally driven by measured voltage behavior; directly copying contact_fault_enable or contact_fault_time_s to the outputs, fabricating Timeseries, or using a disconnected monitoring path is not acceptable. Save the completed model as cand_XBATT09.slx in the submission directory and keep the latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XBATT09.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
